full_judgment: 3. Respondent No. 1 as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 11 of 2001 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Singair, Manikganj for declaration that R.S. record was wrong and also for partition contending, inter-alia, that the suit land belonged to Rashu Pramanik and others. Aditya Pramanik was the tenant under them. Aditya being in possession died leaving behind five sons named Lalit, Mahesh, Krishna, Puma and Gadadhar. C.S. Khatian No. 1356 was correctly prepared in their names. Out of the need for money 5(five) brothers gave 29 decimals of land to Nepal Bepary by korfa pattan. Lalit having died, Paresh Chandra Sarkar, son of Puma Chandra Sarkar got saham of the said 29 decimals of land upon amicable partition. Paresh tried to dispossess Nepal by denying his Korfa pattan. Thereafter, through the settlement of well wishers Paresh executed a kabala on 05.05.1955 but he without registering the same came back and ultimately, the deed was registered through miscellaneous case by presenting the same before the District Registrar. S.A. record was correctly prepared in the name of Nepal but R.S. record was not correctly prepared reflecting his actual share. Nepal died leaving behind two sons, defendant Nos. 1 and 2. Defendant No. 2 sold 8 decimals of land by a registered kabala dated 06.04.1982 to Gadadhar and Kalipada who mutated their names and paid rent. Thereafter, Gadadhar and Kalipada sold 7 decimals of land out of 8 decimals of land to the plaintiff by registered kabala dated 30.06.1992. Defendant No.1 transferred 6 decimals of land to the plaintiff by a kabala dated 30.12.1990. Gadadhar and Kalipada transferred decimal of land to the plaintiff. Though kabala was not registered, possession of the transferred land was handed over. This way the plaintiff is in possession of 14 decimals of land. Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 possess their remaining 15 decimals of land through the plaintiff. The plaintiff sold 4 decimals of land to defendant No.10. The plaintiff has constructed a homestead on the suit land. The defendant having preferred appeal against the mutation order passed in favour of the plaintiff, revenue authority refused to take rent from the plaintiff, hence the, suit.
